question: What was the 2015 Stellar Consensus Protocol rewrite, who authored it, and why did Stellar replace its original consensus?

golden.answer: In 2015 Stellar adopted the Stellar Consensus Protocol, authored by David Mazières, using Federated Byzantine Agreement with node-chosen quorum slices rather than PoW or PoS. SDF announced the paper and code on April 8, and the upgraded network was live on November 3, 2015. Why it replaced the earlier Ripple-derived design is disputed: SDF cited weaknesses the 2014 fork exposed; Ripple said the fork showed no flaw in Ripple consensus.
keyFacts: David Mazières authored the 2015 SCP paper.
SCP is Federated Byzantine Agreement with node-chosen quorum slices, not PoW or PoS.
The upgraded SCP network was live on November 3, 2015.
Why the original consensus was replaced is disputed between SDF and Ripple.
avoid: Do NOT call SCP proof-of-work or proof-of-stake.
Do NOT state SDF’s fork explanation as uncontested fact.
